basics.name: Juanjuan Huang
basics.label: Assistant Beamline Scientist
basics.summary: A multidisciplinary scientist with a Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, Master’s degree materials science and PhD degree in physics, currently working as a beamline scientist at the Advanced Photon Source, Argonne National Laboratory. My expertise lies in developing synchrotron techniques, particularly X-ray spectroscopy and spectral imaging, and applying them to fundamental scientific research.

work.name: Advanced Photon Source, Argonne National Laboratory
work.summary: Develop and operate advanced X-ray spectroscopy and spectral-imaging capabilities at the Advanced Photon Source, maintaining instrumentation, hardware, and software while supporting academic and industrial users across chemistry, materials science, biology, medicine, and physics.

work.name: Advanced Photon Source, Argonne National Laboratory
work.summary: Implemented dispersive, single-acquisition X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) at beamline 25-ID-C, reaching millisecond time resolution per XANES spectrum in the APS Upgrade regime.
highlights: Applied the capability to fast XANES imaging of lithium-ion batteries for the project “Resolving Capacity Fade in Li-Ion Batteries with Single-Shot Chemical Mapping.”
Supervisor: Dr. George Sterbinsky; group leader: Dr. Shelly Kelly.

work.name: Technical University of Munich
work.summary: Developed dispersive XAS capabilities for an inverse Compton source—the first demonstration of XAS with an ICS source worldwide and the fastest high-energy (>20 keV) laboratory XAS at the time—and successfully applied the method to chemical systems.
highlights: Research topic: X-ray absorption spectroscopy at the Munich Compact Light Source.
Supervisors: Prof. Dr. Franz Pfeiffer and Dr. Martin Dierolf; Chair of Biomedical Physics (E17).

work.name: SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory — Stanford Synchrotron Radiation Lightsource
work.summary: Worked at beamline 6-2c, a transmission X-ray microscope, gaining hands-on experience in 3D XANES imaging and data analysis.

work.name: ESRF — The European Synchrotron
work.summary: Completed the thesis “The Electronic Structure of Mononuclear Manganese Compounds: Experimental and Theoretical Insights from X-Ray Absorption Spectroscopy and Resonant Inelastic X-Ray Scattering” at spectroscopy beamline ID26.
highlights: Thesis supervisors: Dr. Marius Retegan and Dr. Pieter Glatzel.

work.name: ESRF — The European Synchrotron
work.summary: Completed an X-ray spectroscopy traineeship at beamline ID26, working on XANES and valence-to-core X-ray emission spectroscopy simulations of transition-metal complexes using ORCA.

volunteer.summary: Lead organizer for the New York City branch of the People's Climate March, the largest climate march in history.
highlights: Awarded 'Climate Hero' award by Greenpeace for my efforts organizing the march.
Men of the year 2014 by Time magazine
